_purpose: Single source of truth for every measured or verified number this project quotes. Documentation must agree with this file; tests/test_docs_consistency.py enforces it. If a number changes, change it HERE and let the tests find every place that disagrees.

subtoken._method: 800 RefChartQA validation images / 1045 boxes; 'sub-token' = narrower than one visual token on at least one axis
subtoken._448_vs_512_cost: Dropping 512 -> 448 removes 29% of visual tokens and costs +9.5 percentage points of sub-token targets overall, +8.5pp on the human subset that carries the published comparison. Measured on RefChartQA validation only (rule 1), 600 rows across all three subsets.

phase2._source: Kaggle Tesla T4, hf_peft backend, 512-pixel budget, single-device pinned (DECISIONS.md 0025). Values below are the POST-FIX run.

_superseded_sharded_run._why: Measured with device_map='auto', which sharded the model across two T4s while torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved() read device 0 alone — understating the footprint by ~3.8x and the step time correspondingly (DECISIONS.md 0025). Kept so the history is legible; never quote these.

gates._gate_revision: Revised from 10 h to 20 h in decision 0034 and disclosed in 0037: the 10 h figure proxied for 'can this finish', which verified resume now answers directly. The revision also ADDED a requirement (resume verified for the exact configuration) that run 11 would have failed.

pinned_revisions._purpose: Exact Hub commit SHAs. Every download passes revision=<sha> so a dataset re-upload cannot silently change what we trained or evaluated on. Non-negotiable rule 6 requires the same dataset VERSION for a matched comparison.
pinned_revisions._api_note: hf_hub_download in huggingface_hub 1.28.0 has NO resume_download parameter - it was removed and downloads always resume. Passing it emits a deprecation warning and is ignored. It DOES take revision, which is what matters here.

sequence_budget._purpose: Measured token costs for the structured output, so Phase 5 prompt design and the max_seq_len setting rest on measurement rather than estimation.
sequence_budget._pretty_printing_penalty: pretty-printed JSON costs 80% more tokens than compact (253 vs 141) for identical content. The prompt must demand compact.
sequence_budget._pad_is_not_eos: pad 151643 != eos 151645, so masking pad tokens does not mask the stop token - the model must still learn to emit <|im_end|>.

phase3._method: 2,500 random ChartQA TRAIN annotations read from the pinned archive (sha256 1bf310e5...), boxes normalised through the same code path the loaders use. Chart-type shares from a separate 3,000-chart sample.

box_value_alignment_r2._note: median r^2 of bar extent against the gold table value, 1,290 series. Lines are excluded: their bboxes are segments between points (85.6% have len(bboxes) == len(y) - 1), so a point's box size is not stated anywhere.

refchartqa_audit._rejected_criterion: relative tightness; gating on it gave 84.0% (human 58.2%) and was disproved against rendered ground truth

image_overlap._method: pixel-content SHA-256 of every ChartQA image (all splits) against 4,000 cached RefChartQA train images

mixtures._rebuilt: 2026-08-28, DECISIONS.md 0072: source pools are filtered through build_target, so every slot trains something. Before this, stage 2 held 3,265 usable records of 12,000.
mixtures._note: stage1_planrich was byte-identical to stage1 — --replay only affects stage 2 — and was deleted rather than kept as a second name for the same file.
mixtures.arms_confound: The plan-rich arm has 10,304 records to the pre-registered arm's 6,304, so a difference between them confounds MORE COMPOSITIONAL SUPERVISION with MORE DATA. The two cannot be separated at this supply: both arms already contain every one of the 4,304 real records that yields a target (DECISIONS.md 0072), so the only way to add compositional plans is to add synthetic ones, which also adds volume. Holding the total fixed caps the contrast at about 1.28x, because 'compositional' means 'not a bare lookup' and a level-balanced 2,000-example replay is already three-quarters compositional. Any reported comparison between the arms must be declared unmatched (PLAN.md 7.4).

phase4._method: Vendored official evaluate.py (sha256 d0c9f87d…) on vendored filtered_results.jsonl against the pinned RefChartQA test split.

level_b_reproduction.cause: filtered_results.jsonl is a FORMAT EXAMPLE, not released predictions (RefChartQA README). No per-model prediction files and no checkpoints are published, so 4.4's premise is unsatisfiable.

stratification._method: 7,158 RefChartQA TRAIN boxes, resized to 512 px long side, token 32 px

extra_box_cost._note: Official torchmetrics path. Free within a single image when ranked last; expensive across a dataset because the official ties every score at 1.0.

reproducible_anchors._finding: The two halves of this project have very different anchor quality, and it is worth stating before any number is produced.

chartqa_answer.claim_level: B, but REACHABLE ONLY AT PHASE 7. The number, the exact checkpoint, the exact prompt and a verified evaluator all exist — but 79.1 is the TEST split, and rule 1 seals test until the pre-registration is committed. The Phase 5.3 baseline is VALIDATION and is not a reproduction of it.

refchartqa_grounding.claim_level: C — cited, not reproducible by anyone (DECISIONS.md 0052)

prompt_iteration._method: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, 4-bit, 512 px, T4, frozen ChartQA validation slice. PLAN 5.1 iterates on validation only.

v1_pretty_printed._note: 4 of 5 failures were truncation at the 512 cap

v2_compact._note: compaction cut tokens 2.6x; schema failures then became the binding constraint — args too long, duplicate labels, unit too long, op 'average'

v3_schema_limits_stated._note: schema limits stated and the cap raised to 900 did not move validity: the remaining failures are two syntax slips (a stray quote after a bbox array, 11-21 per affected record; and model_answer nested inside plan) plus run-on enumeration on long charts

chartqa_table_rows._why_it_matters: OUTPUT_SCHEMA caps evidence at 8, deliberately, because extra boxes cost AP (DECISIONS.md 0014). The majority of charts have more elements than that, so a whole-chart aggregate cannot be both fully grounded and fully executable.

evidence_cap_impact._method: 340 mined ChartQA training plans replayed through the executor with the evidence list truncated to MAX_EVIDENCE=8
evidence_cap_impact._note: Corrects an overstated concern in DECISIONS.md 0060. Tables are long (median 10 rows) but questions with a UNIQUE executable plan need very little evidence, so the cap does not bind for them.

scoring_path_verified._method: 30 real RefChartQA validation rows, oracle predictions, scored through the vendored official evaluate.py — no GPU
scoring_path_verified._why: Verifies every convention between a streamed row and the reported number: {x,y,w,h} ground truth, normalised 0-1000 boxes, clamping, the <box>...<grounding-sep> emitter, and analyse_dataset. An error anywhere in that chain would look like a mediocre model result.

refchartqa_val_gt_boxes_per_row._note: the 8-evidence cap does not bind here

variant_selection_5_2._method: frozen 200-question ChartQA validation slice, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, 4-bit, 512 px, T4. Adequately powered: n=200 resolves ~10 points.
variant_selection_5_2._note: The n=24 probes had reported round-trip at 40-50%; at n=200 it is 69%, confirming DECISIONS.md 0062 that the small probes were noise.
variant_selection_5_2._denominators: relaxed_accuracy, valid_json and schema_valid are over all 200 questions; roundtrip_agreement and roundtrip_executable are over the 71 schema-valid records only (49/71 and 67/71). Re-scored on the 93 post-repair schema-valid records they are 65.6% and 84.9%.

target_quality._method: 636 ChartQA training records and 1,500 RefChartQA records, targets built and required to parse, satisfy OUTPUT_SCHEMA, and round-trip
defects_found: RefChartQA targets used null values with a lookup plan: 100% failed round-trip
evidence was the first 8 boxes, not the labels the plan references
build_mixtures.py dropped meta['elements'], so all labels were placeholders
values read from the annotation while the plan was verified on the table

early_stopping._why_not_ap: AP needs generation. At 6 evaluations in a 3,000-step run the 95% CI is +/-12.2 pts at n=64, +/-8.7 at n=128, and only +/-4.9 at n=400 which costs 5.3 h against ~10 h of training. An AP that cannot detect 'has not improved' would stop on noise (DECISIONS.md 0069).

evidence_cap._method: RefChartQA train, the 200-record audit sample in data/refchartqa_audit.jsonl (n_boxes_raw, before any cap)
evidence_cap._why: MAX_EVIDENCE = 8 caps how many boxes a training target can carry. If most records exceeded it the cap would put a ceiling on recall, and so on AP, for reasons unrelated to the model.
evidence_cap._finding: The cap binds on 2% of records. It is a bounded, small cost, not a structural ceiling on AP.

supervision_supply._method: scripts/measure_target_yield.py --source <name>, CPU only. A record is 'usable' when build_target succeeds: it parses, satisfies OUTPUT_SCHEMA, and its plan reproduces its own answer against its own evidence.
supervision_supply._measured: 2026-08-28, after the three fixes in DECISIONS.md 0071

chartqa_train._binding: 19,634 have no mined plan and none can be derived

refchartqa_train_cached._note: only 7% of the split is cached; the PLAN 3.x scaling ladder at 10,000/25,000 rows needs more, and caching is CPU and bandwidth only

supervision_supply._finding: The whole supply of REAL chart supervision this project can build is 4,483 records. Synthetic supplies the rest, which is why Change 2's synthetic-to-real transfer claim (PLAN 9.4) carries the weight it does.
